description: The value an insurance company or jury will put on a child's facial scars depends on the quality of the documentation provided by you and your attorney.
shortAnswer: The value an insurance company or jury will put on a child's scars will depend on the quality of the documentation provided by you and your attorney. Another component of the value on your child's scar claim is the cost of future treatment.

faq.q: When is the best time to photograph my child's scar for an injury claim?
faq.a: Scars sometimes fade with time and the insurance companies know this. The best time to photograph or video your child's scars will be after your plastic surgeon or dermatologist tells you their appearance/function is not going to improve further.

faq.q: What if photos don't show how a facial scar affects my child?
faq.a: Some facial scarring is more noticeable when a child is talking, smiling, laughing or blinking, and still photography will not capture the full impact. It may be best to allow the insurance company to meet and interact with your child, or a videographer can be hired to film a “Day-In-The-Life” video.

faq.q: Does gender affect the value of a child's scarring injury?
faq.a: Gender also affects the value of a scarring injury. For better or worse, boys tend to receive less than girls for the same type of scarring.

faq.q: How much can future treatment costs add to a child's scar claim?
faq.a: For one child client, her plastic surgeon provided a long list of future treatment, including PhotoDerm pulsed light therapy, Microdermabrasion, Fat or synthetic grafting, an Endoscopic unilateral brow lift, and Botox every 4 months for life. Those future medical costs added approximately $50,000.00 of value to my client's claim.
